balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

netIncomeBridge.title: Net income vs net income ordinary, NCI and perpetual-bond profit
netIncomeBridge.content:
Under PRC CAS (effective FY2025, with these specific disclosures populated FY2021-FY2024), the reported net income line already nets out the profit attributable to non-controlling interests, but perpetual bonds are classified as an equity instrument, so the coupon paid to perpetual-bond holders (perpetual bond profit) is counted as a profit distribution rather than an interest expense -- it stays inside equity and inside the net-income-to-equity flow that ordinary shareholders' EPS is built from. Net income ordinary strips that coupon back out, and minority interest profit shows separately how much of consolidated profit (overseas Shanjin International, 71% NCI; Veladero, 50% NCI) never reaches Shandong Gold's own shareholders at all.

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: the DCF deducts the CNY ~14bn perpetual-bond balance from equity value because it ranks senior to ordinary equity, and uses a combined 49.6% leakage rate (30% cash tax x 28% NCI) rather than this reported split, precisely because NetIncomeOrdinary is not yet disclosed for FY2025.

What to watch:

  • Perpetual bond profit rising faster than net income -- more of the coupon burden sitting ahead of ordinary holders
  • Minority interest profit's share of the total, as Shanjin International and Veladero scale
  • The FY2025 gap in this chart: the split is not yet broken out in the filings read so far

perpetualBonds.title: Perpetual bonds outstanding
perpetualBonds.content:
Perpetual bonds (CAS: "other equity instruments") are a debt-like claim classified inside equity -- they carry a coupon but have no maturity date, so they never force repayment, yet they are economically senior to ordinary shareholders in any wind-down.

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: the balance grew from zero (FY2019) to CNY ~14bn (H1 2026), funding the overseas and domestic capex buildout alongside bank debt and the 2025 equity placing. The DCF's equity bridge deducts this balance from enterprise value before arriving at ordinary equity value -- it is why the base-case intrinsic value is a thin residual rather than a simple EV-less-net-debt figure.

What to watch:

  • The balance still growing faster than equity -- more senior leakage ahead of ordinary holders
  • Coupon rate resets or new issuance in future filings

ocfBasis.title: Operating cash flow: IFRS vs CAS basis
ocfBasis.content:
Shandong Gold switched its primary financial statements from IFRS to PRC GAAP (CAS) starting with the FY2025 annual report; every quarterly and half-year filing since is CAS only. Operating cash flow here is the IFRS-era figure as originally reported; operating cash flow (CAS, restated) is the CAS figure for the same fiscal year where both exist.

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: FY2024 operating cash flow is RMB20.3bn under IFRS but RMB13.3bn under CAS for the identical twelve months -- a ~34% gap from classification differences alone, not a change in the underlying business. Comparing any pre-FY2025 OCF print directly against FY2025 OCF overstates the swing.

What to watch:

  • Treat FY2025 onward as its own CAS series, not a continuation of the IFRS one
  • The DCF anchors its FY0 capex/D&A/EBITDA base entirely on the FY2025 CAS statements for this reason

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Shandong Gold Mining Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
